newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA TRANSNET FINDS ALLEGED CREDIT CARD FRAUDS.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA TRANSNET FINDS ALLEGED CREDIT CARD FRAUDS.

text.p: South African transport parastatal Transnet said on Tuesday that it had uncovered 121 cases of alleged credit card fraud by its employees.
The firm launched an investigation in April last year which was conducted by external auditors and overseen by the head of Transnet's internal audit unit.
"The investigation identified a total of 121 cases of... abuse of company credit cards," the firm said in a statement.
There are 4,000 credit card holders in the firm and a moratorium had been offered for offenders -- but no one took up the offer.
Charge sheets have already been prepared to deal with the alleged offenders who will appear before disciplinary inquiry panels before the end of this month.
"In appropriate cases criminal charges will be instituted and the losses recovered," the firm said.
The alleged frauds ranged from frequent cash withdrawals and private expenditure to the forging of vouchers.
A Transnet spokeswoman said the total sum involved in the frauds was not currently being divulged and that the investigation was still ongoing.
"This is just a first phase in the investigation, more details will follow later," she said.
Transnet introduced a new system of credit card control on July 1 this year.
